findings.problem: A route table given with `start --routes` (or an edit of the run folder's routes.json) can replace the official route that official-only mode runs for a CONFIRMED terms_restricted host. YouTube pages are then read through an arbitrary third-party host (for example an Invidious/Piped-style mirror) as an 'official route', although youtube-terms is confirmed and 'never lifted'. More generally a custom table can put any host, including a reader proxy via the {url_enc} template variable, into an 'official' feed/oembed route for any URL. This contradicts the promise that the packaged lists always apply and that a custom table can only add restrictions.
findings.evidence: _terms_stop() takes the platform from the run's own table: `platform, values = st.routes.match(st.url)` (ladder.py:947), Routes() is built from run.routes (ladder.py:341-345, read():1104), and _rung0() expands any feed/oembed url template with no host binding for no-key routes (ladder.py:865-887; {url_enc} at ladder.py:152). key_for() binds only keys, not route hosts. Test scratchpad/review/r1/t_routes_mirror.py: a table whose 'youtube' platform has official=[{kind:feed, url:'http://mirror.test:PORT/feed/{video}'}] gives `read https://www.youtube.com/shorts/dQw4w9WgXcQ` exit 0, bucket read, rung R0, reasons ['official:feed','route:youtube','official_only'], access_basis public_anonymous, terms {entry: youtube-terms, status: confirmed, lifted: false, mode: official_only}; the mirror served /feed/dQw4w9WgXcQ. The same happens with no --routes after editing <run>/routes.json (routes sha256 in run.json is never re-checked). Promise contradicted: scope.py:26-28, public-page-access.md:197-200 and 850, routes.json note.
findings.fix: For a terms_restricted URL take the platform and its official routes from the PACKAGED table only (scope.packaged()), never from the run table; bind every official route's host (key or no key) to the hosts the packaged table names for it, as key_for() does for keys; refuse custom official routes whose template host is not on the page's registrable domain (and forbid {url}/{url_enc} in custom route hosts' paths unless same-site); verify the run's routes.json and brief hashes against run.json on every command. Add a test: a custom table cannot change what official-only mode reads.

findings.problem: One terms check lifts two different restrictions, including the Naver Cafe (mom cafe) bulk-collection notice. (a) A check the user writes for Naver's general terms (host naver.com, terms_url policy.naver.com) also lifts naver-cafe-bulk-notice for cafe.naver.com and m.cafe.naver.com, because a check covers every subdomain and the cafe entry is the first entry that matches cafe hosts. (b) A check for cafe.naver.com lifts the cafe entry and thereby also naver-terms for cafe hosts, because only the FIRST matching entry is consulted. `start` and `close` misreport it: describe_checks says only 'lifts naver-terms', and urls_under_lift does not count the cafe reads. D1 requires a terms_checked item 'for that host' per entry; the owner named mom cafes explicitly.
findings.evidence: terms_entry() returns the first entry whose hosts match (scope.py:183-188); terms_check() matches the check host as a suffix (scope.py:191-198); evaluate() consults one entry (scope.py:258-265). Entry order: naver-cafe-bulk-notice (routes.json:458) before naver-terms (routes.json:472), both covering cafe.naver.com. Test scratchpad/review/r1/t_terms.py, run 'naver-lift' (checks for naver.com and youtube.com): start prints [{host: naver.com, entry: naver-terms, effect: 'lifts naver-terms (reported) ...'}], yet `read https://cafe.naver.com/imsanbu/123` is no longer stopped (the reader looks up cafe.naver.com, i.e. it would request it). Run 'cafe-lift' (check for cafe.naver.com only): cafe.naver.com is not stopped although naver-terms also covers it. summary() counts lifts by the URL's entry id (ledger.py:753) while check rows carry the check's entry (ledger.py:762-764), so cafe reads under the naver.com check are not attributed.
findings.fix: Evaluate every terms entry that covers the host and require each to be lifted; make a check name the entry it lifts (an `entry` field, validated against the packaged ids) and match terms_url to that entry's terms_url or sources; never let a check on a parent host lift a more specific entry; make describe_checks list every entry a check lifts and every entry it does not. Add tests for both directions.

findings.problem: The robots.txt fetch follows redirects with no scope check, so a robots.txt that redirects sends a request to a terms_restricted host, a denied host or a private channel. This breaks 'Nothing is requested from a terms_restricted host, not even its robots.txt' and 'every redirect hop gets the same checks'. Short-link and alias hosts (see L-15) are the likely trigger.
findings.evidence: robots_decision() calls net.fetch(origin + '/robots.txt', ...) without on_redirect (ladder.py:446-448); net.fetch then follows every hop (net.py:484-515), checking only SSRF. Test scratchpad/review/r1/t_robots_redirect.py: short.test/robots.txt answers 302 -> https://www.youtube.com/robots.txt; `read http://short.test:PORT/post/1` produced a DNS lookup of www.youtube.com (harness log) and ended 'unread: www.youtube.com did not resolve' - with real DNS it would have fetched YouTube's robots.txt. `robots http://denyhop.test/page` with --deny-host denied.test fetched denied.test/robots.txt (server log). Promise: public-page-access.md:742 and 17.2; ladder.py docstring 43-46.
findings.fix: Pass an on_redirect callback to the robots fetch that refuses any hop scope_stop() stops (deny, search page, never_call, private, terms) and treat a refused robots redirect conservatively (record the origin's robots as unreachable/disallowed, or stop the URL with the hop's scope class). Add the short-link and deny-host cases to the tests.

findings.problem: Archive, cache, translation-proxy, reader-proxy and front-end-mirror URLs that wrap a terms_restricted or private URL pass every scope check, so `read`/`robots`/`ingest` fetch or accept them. The docs forbid this (SKILL.md:99, public-page-access.md:313-317 and 493-495) but nothing in code enforces it, although the whole design is 'decided from the URL alone'. A page's injected text (or a search result) can steer the agent to such a URL. `allow_wayback_for_official` defaults to true and is not scoped by any code.
findings.evidence: scope.evaluate() looks only at the URL's own host (scope.py:230-265). Offline check with the packaged lists returned no stop for: web.archive.org/web/2026/https://gall.dcinside.com/board/view/?id=...; web.archive.org/web/2026id_/https://cafe.naver.com/imsanbu/123; archive.ph/newest/https://www.coupang.com/vp/products/123; gall-dcinside-com.translate.goog/...; m-youtube-com.translate.goog/watch?v=...; cafe-naver-com.translate.goog/imsanbu/123; r.jina.ai/https://gall.dcinside.com/...; m-dcinside-com.cdn.ampproject.org/c/s/m.dcinside.com/...; yewtu.be/watch?v=...; piped.video/watch?v=.... allow_wayback_for_official: ledger.py:276,286, schema line 94, public-page-access.md:489-491 (only recorded, never applied).
findings.fix: Add a packaged 'wrapper' list (web.archive.org, archive.today/ph/is, *.translate.goog, cdn.ampproject.org, r.jina.ai and other reader proxies, webcache/cache hosts, known YouTube/Reddit/X front ends) and in scope.evaluate() extract the embedded target (path/query URL, or the translate.goog label encoding) and apply every scope list to it; refuse wrapper URLs whose target is scoped (exit 2), and refuse proxies/front ends outright. Scope Wayback use in code to the product's own domains (brief.product.url) and only when the embedded URL passes the scope checks.

findings.problem: Host-wide stops (human check, second rate-limit signal, three unreadable URLs, and the planned bot_filter/js_check stops) are keyed by the exact hostname. The same site's other hosts - m., www., the apex - keep being read after the stop, which is reading around a human check or a rate limit through 'another host' (forbidden by public-page-access.md section 7). The R2 generic www.->m. rewrite automates exactly this sibling switch for later URLs.
findings.evidence: host_stop()/acquire() look up state['hosts'][host] by exact host (ledger.py:498-501, 503-515); read() checks run.host_stop(host) for the URL's own host only (ladder.py:1120). Test scratchpad/review/r1/t_sibling_host.py: www.site.test answers with a reCAPTCHA widget -> human_check and host stop; then `read http://m.site.test/p2` -> exit 0 read and `read http://site.test/p2` -> exit 0 read. www.rl.test answers 429 twice -> host stopped (rate_limit); `read http://m.rl.test/b` -> exit 0 read. Generic rewrite: ladder.py:987-996.
findings.fix: Key run-level stops (human_check, rate_limit, bot_filter_persistent and the new bot_filter/js_check stops) by registrable domain (ladder.registrable_domain) and check them in read, ingest, robots and _request (alternates and official routes on the same site). Keep key_rejected per API host. Add tests for www->m and apex after a stop.

findings.problem: When robots.txt is answered by a challenge or bot-filter page, the reader records 'unavailable_bot_filtered' and treats the whole host as allowed. The `robots` command - documented as the gate that says whether a browser tool may open a host - then exits 0 'allowed' for a host that has just shown the reader a bot check, and a real browser will pass that check. A bot check at the door is a refusal, not permission.
findings.evidence: record_from_fetch(): `elif challenge: record['status'] = 'unavailable_bot_filtered'` (robots.py:253-254); decide(): any status other than ok/unreachable -> allowed (robots.py:281-282); ladder.py:454-466 sets challenge from verdict.robots_challenge(). Documented: public-page-access.md:400-402 ('A bot-filter page served instead of robots.txt is unavailable_bot_filtered: reading is allowed'). Test scratchpad/review/r1/t_robots_redirect.py: guarded.test/robots.txt answers 403 with a 'Checking your browser' page -> `robots` exit 0, allowed True, robots_status unavailable_bot_filtered, http_status 403.
findings.fix: Treat a challenge served for robots.txt as a host-wide check stop for the run (human_check when a widget shows, otherwise the new bot check stop), make `robots` exit 3 for it, and update public-page-access.md section 9 and the vocabulary.

findings.problem: The recorded clauses of the reported entries allow collection only with prior (written) permission or consent, so `permits_this_reading` can honestly be true only if the user holds that permission - yet a lift is a bare self-attestation with no field for the permission and an optional note. DC Inside's 제16조 (read on its own domain) bars crawling 'in any form or for any purpose without prior written consent'; naver-terms bars automated collection 'without Naver's prior permission'; the cafe notice bars bulk collection 'without the consent of members and the cafe'; the Coupang clause bars automated agents/scripts. D1 keeps DC Inside 'reported' (owner decision, flagged as an open item by the implementing lanes); under the standing instruction that DC Inside and mom cafes must never have a reason to sue, this needs the owner's explicit re-confirmation.
findings.evidence: routes.json:444-456 (dcinside-terms clause and status reported), 458-470 (naver-cafe-bulk-notice), 472-484 (naver-terms), 486-500 (coupang-terms). scope.py:49-50 CHECK_FIELDS/CHECK_REQUIRED have no permission field; terms_record() lifts on result alone (scope.py:201-219). platform-map.md dcinside row: '사용자가 원문을 읽고 이번 읽기가 허용된다고 판단해 기록한 실행에서만 풀림'. implement-results open issue: 'DC Inside stays reported by owner decision even though its 제16조 bars crawling without prior written consent'.
findings.fix: Owner decision: either mark dcinside-terms confirmed (its clause was read), or add a per-entry `requires_permission: true` and make a lift require a `permission_ref` (who granted written consent, date, reference) in the terms check; say in 17.5, L16 and the platform map that 'permits_this_reading' for these entries means written permission, not the user's reading of public-page rules.

findings.problem: The YouTube Data API route's policy note, public-page-access 17.4 and legal-checklist L17 cover only the 30-day and protected-attribute rules. The Developer Policies also say API clients must not 'access or use API Data to create new or derived data or metrics' unless approved (the derived-metrics policy applies only to audited developers who applied through the quota-extension process from 2026-06-01, and lists 'viewer sentiment analysis' and 'content categorization and tagging' as such metrics). Coding comments into pain points, sentiment or counts - the pack's purpose - may fall under this. The user's own obligations as the API client (accepting the API ToS, privacy-policy and compliance-audit requirements) are not mentioned either. L17 even cites the derived-metrics-policy URL without stating its content.
findings.evidence: routes.json:249 policy_note (30 days, protected attributes only); public-page-access.md section 17.4; legal-checklist.md:541-563 (L17 lists developer-policies and derived-metrics-policy URLs but describes only storage and protected attributes). Search-index text of developers.google.com/youtube/terms/developer-policies: 'Your API Clients must not (i) replace API Data with similar, independently calculated data, or (ii) access or use API Data to create new or derived data or metrics'; of .../derived-metrics-policy: 'only applicable to audited developers with analytics use cases that have explicitly applied for permission ... (starting June 01, 2026)', examples 'content categorization and tagging, viewer sentiment analysis'. Direct fetch of developers.google.com was blocked here (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the primary text was not read.
findings.fix: Add the derived-data rule to the route's policy_note, 17.4, L17 (marked 미확인(요약), 법률가 판단/counsel decides) and the platform map; until counsel or the owner decides, restrict YouTube API items to qualitative evidence (paraphrase, short quotes as existence evidence) with no sentiment, category or count metrics computed from them, or require the user to confirm in the brief that their API project is approved for such use; tell the user that their key binds them to the YouTube API ToS and Developer Policies.

findings.problem: `ingest` refuses captures only when the host is stopped for rate_limit or human_check. After any other host-wide stop - bot_filter_persistent, key_rejected, and whatever class the planned bot_filter/js_check host stops get - a render capture of a URL that was read before the stop is still taken in, i.e. a capture can follow a host-wide refusal. This also undermines the decided change ('ingest will refuse captures that passed through any check') unless this list is updated.
findings.evidence: ladder.py:1377-1381: `if stopped and stopped.get('class') in ('rate_limit', 'human_check'): return _ingest_stopped(...)`; _capture_blocked() looks only at the URL's own earlier outcomes (ladder.py:1281-1307), so a URL read 'unread' before the host stop passes. bot_filter_persistent is set in note_outcome() (ledger.py:606-619).
findings.fix: Refuse every capture on a host (and, per L-05, a site) that carries any run-level stop; add a test for bot_filter_persistent and for the new check stop classes.

findings.problem: Redirect loops and similar fetch failures leave the URL 'unread' with R3 untried and the ingest help text, so the researcher renders it in a real browser and the capture is accepted. A self-redirect or cookie-setting redirect loop is a common bot/cookie check; a browser (which keeps cookies) passes it. This is another way past a check that the decided bot_filter/js_check change does not cover, because a redirect loop never becomes a verdict.
findings.evidence: net.fetch raises NetError('redirect_loop') when a target repeats (net.py:507-509); _request marks it contacted (ladder.py:551-552); _error_outcome() returns bucket 'unread', untried ['R3'], next_step INGEST_HELP (ladder.py:792-803); _capture_blocked() accepts an unread, contacted prior read (ladder.py:1287-1300). Documented: public-page-access.md:262-266 ('Fetch failures are not stops ... redirect_loop ... leave the URL unread (exit 4)').
findings.fix: Treat redirect_loop (at least loops that return to the requested URL or set cookies) as a check stop - no R2/R3 and no capture - and state it in section 5; keep too_large and decode errors as unread.

findings.problem: A capture declared `--context unknown` is recorded as public_anonymous, and class-1 tools (the user's own, usually signed-in browser) are the documented first choice 'for R3 captures'. For a member-only page whose anonymous pre-read ended unread rather than auth_gate (a JS-shell page such as an SPA cafe article, which still escalates after the decided change), a signed-in render can be taken in as public content whenever the signed-in markers are not recognised - past the membership gate, outside signed_in_communities.
findings.evidence: CONTEXTS includes 'unknown' (ladder.py:104); for context != signed_in no community is looked up (ladder.py:1329); basis = 'public_anonymous' for any non-authorised read (ladder.py:1407). Class 1 'Interactive browsing and R3 captures' (public-page-access.md:44) and 'usually with the user's sign-ins' (line 66); section 10 step 6 allows `unknown` (line 433). The backstop detects only logout links/lines and greetings (verdict.py:382-393; public-page-access.md section 3 says it cannot recognise every signed-in view).
findings.fix: Treat `unknown` as signed-in: refuse it unless the URL is in an authorised community (then summary_only), or record it with a non-public access basis that cannot support claims; limit R3 captures to class-2 fresh profiles or a confirmed private window and drop 'R3 captures' from class 1's use.

findings.problem: A rate-limit notice (for example '요청이 너무 많습니다' on a 200 page) and a human-check notice without a widget or error status stop only their own URL: no wait is imposed and the host keeps being requested at normal pace. Continuing to call a host that just said it is rate-limiting or checking for bots is getting past the rate limit/check.
findings.evidence: verdict.py:624-625 returns rate_limit with 'word_only' and host_wide False; verdict.py:614-618 makes a word-only human_check host_wide only when a widget or status >= 400 backs it; _terminal() stops the host only when host_wide (ladder.py:824-831); _host_signal() requires host_wide (ladder.py:818-821). Documented: public-page-access.md:231 ('A notice alone: its URL only').
findings.fix: Count every rate-limit notice as a host signal (one wait, then the host/site stops), as captures already do, and make a human-check notice stop the host (site) for the run.

findings.problem: X (Twitter) is routed like an open site - oEmbed at R0, then a plain R1 GET of x.com/twitter.com pages and render captures - with no terms_restricted entry, although X's Terms of Service (in force since 2023-09-29) state that 'crawling or scraping the Services in any form, for any purpose without our prior written consent is expressly prohibited' and set liquidated damages per 1,000,000 posts. X Corp litigates against scrapers, so this is a 'similar site' under the owner's standing instruction. The route predates this change, but the new terms_restricted mechanism was not applied to it.
findings.evidence: routes.json:336 platform 'x' (hosts x.com, twitter.com, mobile.twitter.com; official oEmbed at publish.twitter.com; no terms entry in routes.json:386-500); public-page-access.md section 14 X row ('R0 oEmbed for a single public post'). ToS wording read only through search results (Yahoo Finance/TechCrunch report of the 2023 update, news.ycombinator.com/item?id=37433759, X ToS PDF 2025-05-08 listed in results); the primary PDF on cdn.cms-twdigitalassets.com was blocked here.
findings.fix: Add an x-terms entry (hosts x.com, twitter.com, t.co and the other X hosts) as reported now and confirmed once a person reads the clause; decide explicitly whether oEmbed at publish.twitter.com may stay as its official_route (official-only mode) under X's developer terms, otherwise no route. Review the other non-Korean rows (Reddit, Bluesky, Hacker News, stores) the same way.

findings.problem: Collateral of the already-decided bot_filter/js_check change: several places outside public-page-access.md section 10 still tell the agent to pass self-clearing checks or to escalate after a refusal, and will contradict the new rule unless changed together: the ingest help text shown to the agent ('let a self-clearing check finish (at most 15 s)'), SKILL.md's 'any check that does not clear by itself', section 1's 'a page that refuses a scripted request but shows in that private window is still public, and the reader ladder applies', the section 5 verdict table, community-to-test.md's route cells ('Then the R2 mobile twin' for DC Inside, 'the R2 mobile twin, or an R3 render' for Naver Cafes, 'R1, the R2 mobile twin ..., or an R3 render' for other forums), and the bundled page reader, which waits up to 15 s for a self-clearing check.
findings.evidence: ladder.py:96-99 (INGEST_HELP); SKILL.md:79-80; public-page-access.md:24-29, 214-215; references/persona-qa/community-to-test.md:72-75; README.md:101-104 and README.ko.md:77 (ladder ending in a real-browser render); korea/platform-map.md:52 ('필요하면 익명 브라우저 렌더 뒤 ingest'); drivers/web/read_page.mjs:12-13, 240-249 (outside this diff, owned by another session).
findings.fix: Change these texts in the same commit as the decided change: no waiting for any check, no render after a refusal, no route cell that points at a mobile twin or a render as the way in; have read_page.mjs stop (exit 3) on any check marker instead of waiting.

findings.problem: Short-link and alias hosts of restricted operators are not in the terms entries, so a robots.txt fetch and a GET go to the operator before the stop at the redirect hop (and via L-03 the robots.txt redirect itself can reach the restricted host). D1 asks for a stop before any request; youtu.be was added, but naver.me and me2.do (Naver), coupa.ng (Coupang Partners), youtubekids.com (YouTube Kids) and Meta short hosts such as ig.me and m.me were not.
findings.evidence: Test scratchpad/review/r1/t_terms.py (no network allowed): read/robots of https://naver.me/xAbCdE, https://me2.do/xAbCdE and https://coupa.ng/abc each produced a DNS lookup (getaddrinfo naver.me / me2.do / coupa.ng) instead of a terms stop, while every listed host (youtube.com, m./music., youtu.be, shorts, youtube-nocookie.com, instagram.com, instagr.am, threads.com/.net, facebook.com, m./web./l.facebook.com, fb.com, fb.me, fb.watch, dcinside.com and subdomains, cafe/blog/kin/m.place/smartstore.naver.com, rss.blog.naver.com, coupang.com, link.coupang.com) stopped with zero network events. routes.json:386-500 host lists.
findings.fix: Add the operators' short-link and alias hosts to their entries after confirming ownership (naver.me, me2.do; coupa.ng; youtubekids.com and any country domains that resolve; ig.me, m.me, messenger.com if in scope), and add them to the terms tests.

findings.problem: A signed-in greeting line from a capture, which contains a member's (often the researcher's own) name, is copied verbatim into the result's reasons, printed to the agent in the stderr summary and written to the ledger, where it survives `close` (close cuts only URL fields). Page text of that capture is discarded, but the name is kept.
findings.evidence: _logged_in(): `reasons.append(f'line:{value}')` (verdict.py:391); ingest puts v.reasons into the result and the ledger outcome (ladder.py:1415, 1443); _strip_ledger_urls() cuts only URL keys (ledger.py:771-800). Test scratchpad/review/r1/t_privacy.py: a capture with '김민지님 환영합니다' -> reasons ['capture:signed_in_view','href:logout','line:김민지님 환영합니다']; the name is in the stderr summary and in access-ledger.jsonl before and after close.
findings.fix: Record 'line:greeting' / 'line:logout' without the page text (or scrub the line before recording) and strip free-text reasons at close.

findings.problem: Partial-IP scrubbing and the author-key refusal cover only the DC Inside suffix form '(a.b)'. Masked or other placements used by other boards pass both: '211.36.***.***', '118.235.xxx.xxx', '118.235.*.*', '(IP 118.235)', and handles with the IP in front, in brackets or after a space are keyed. D9 requires partial IPs removed before the model sees text.
findings.evidence: privacy.py:82-83 (ip needs four numeric octets; partial_ip only '(d.d)'), privacy.py:193 (_TRAILING_IP only at the end in parentheses). Offline: scrub('작성자 IP: 211.36.***.***'), scrub('ㅇㅇ(118.235.xxx.xxx)'), scrub('118.235.*.* 에서 작성'), scrub('(IP 118.235)') all return the text unchanged; author-key accepts '(118.235)고양이', '고양이[118.235]', '고양이 118.235' (test scratchpad/review/r1/t_privacy.py).
findings.fix: Add masked-octet patterns (digits or *, x, X, ● groups) and 'IP' labels to the partial_ip scrub, and refuse handles that contain an IP-like fragment anywhere.

findings.problem: For non-API sources the capture record and the audience file keep condition (health, disability) and age cues in the same record as the author key, contradicting workflow.md ('Never record a protected attribute against an author key'; health, disability and age only in segment-level claims) and legal-checklist L10 (개인정보 보호법 제23조① treats health as 민감정보). The carve-out exists only for official-API sources.
findings.evidence: research-protocol.md:100-103 (retention, author key and 'Segment, context, task, condition and device cues' in one record) and :118 (prohibition only 'for a source read through an official API'); audience-pipeline.md:247-248 (sources carry author_key; excerpts carry condition cues; carve-out only for official API excerpts); workflow.md:22; legal-checklist.md L10.
findings.fix: Apply the rule to every source: protected-attribute cues (health, disability, age, and the other protected attributes) are never stored in an author-keyed record; attach them only to segment-level claims or to excerpts stripped of author and thread keys.

findings.problem: After a lift the 10-document budget is counted per exact hostname, not per terms entry, so one naver.com lift allows 10 documents on each Naver subdomain (cafe, m.cafe, blog, m.blog, kin, m.kin, m.place, smartstore, ...), and R2 alternates add their own 10. For a bulk-collection notice (Naver Cafe) the cap should bound the whole entry.
findings.evidence: host_limit() applies LIFTED_HOST_BUDGET to the host string (ledger.py:450-456) with per-host counters entry['docs'] (ledger.py:530, 559); scope.lifted_host() is per host (scope.py:268-271).
findings.fix: Count lifted documents per terms entry (and per site), e.g. a counter keyed by the entry id checked in acquire() and book_render().

findings.problem: A terms check has no lower bound or maximum age: a check dated before the restriction existed still lifts it (for example a check of cafe.naver.com dated 2026-01-01 lifts the 2026-08-31 bulk-collection notice), and a years-old check lifts an entry whose terms may have changed.
findings.evidence: validate_checks() only refuses checked_on after today (scope.py:308-336, the check at 335); terms_record() ignores dates (scope.py:201-219); the lanes left 'No maximum age is enforced on terms_checked.checked_on' as an open item.
findings.fix: Refuse (or do not lift with) a check older than the entry's checked_at/restriction date or older than a maximum age (for example 90 days, the pack's own re-check interval).

findings.problem: The run's policy (terms_checked, signed_in_communities, deny_hosts) and route table are read from run.json and routes.json on every command without re-validation or hash checks, so an agent that edits the run folder (for example after injected page text) can add a lift or an authorised community, or change routes (L-01), and the reader honours it. 'Only the user's brief carries terms checks' is enforced only at `start`.
findings.evidence: Run.__init__ sets self.policy = self.meta['policy'] (ledger.py:403); the routes property reads routes.json as is (ledger.py:423-427); brief_sha256 and the routes sha256 are recorded at create() (ledger.py:363, 373) and never compared; scope.evaluate() uses run.policy directly.
findings.fix: On every command re-read brief.json, verify both hashes against run.json, re-derive and re-validate the policy from the brief, and refuse a run whose files changed.

findings.problem: Both READMEs (and the L17 summary row) state as fact that YouTube API items are deleted after 30 days, but nothing deletes bundle items: page files go after 72 h/close, while retention_until enforcement waits for the deferred gate (D13). A user reading the README may believe the tool keeps them within the YouTube 30-day rule.
findings.evidence: README.ko.md:96 ('기한이 지나면 지웁니다'); README.md:151 ('Items from the API are kept 30 days'); legal-checklist.md:99; enforcement deferred per implement-results (code:youtube-api open issue 'retention_until is stamped but not enforced downstream').
findings.fix: Say that the user must delete or re-read each item by its retention_until until the planned gate enforces it.

findings.problem: The search-results refusal list covers only eight engines, while the docs forbid all search result pages; for example search.brave.com, www.ecosia.org/search, www.startpage.com, yandex.*/search, www.baidu.com/s and search.nate.com would be read.
findings.evidence: routes.json:366-385 search_pages (search.naver.com, search.daum.net, search.zum.com, google.com/search, google.co.kr/search, bing.com/search, search.yahoo.com, duckduckgo.com?q=); public-page-access.md section 7 ('Never load search-engine result pages').
findings.fix: Extend search_pages (and a test) to the other common engines and Korean portals, or refuse any URL whose path/query has the shape of a results page on a known engine host.

summary: All listed restricted hosts (DC Inside, Naver incl. cafe/blog/kin/place/smartstore/RSS and m. hosts, Coupang incl. link., YouTube incl. m./music./shorts/youtu.be/nocookie, Instagram, Threads .com/.net, Facebook incl. fb.com/fb.me/fb.watch/m./l.) stop before any request in read, robots and ingest, with zero network I/O in an offline harness; a brief cannot lift a confirmed entry; legal text (legal-checklist, kwcag law layer) is accurate against the mirrors, carries 법률 자문 아님, 미확인 labels and counsel-decides marks, and its 2021도1533 description matches the judgment; S2/S3 wording is clean; no copied third-party text found; the YouTube key never leaks and no channel IDs are stored. But two blockers get past terms stops: a custom or edited route table can swap YouTube's official-only route for a mirror (read exit 0 on a confirmed entry), and a Naver terms check silently lifts the Naver Cafe/mom-cafe notice (and vice versa). Majors: robots.txt redirects reach restricted/denied hosts; archive/translate/proxy wrapper URLs pass all scope checks; host stops don't cover the same site's m./www./apex hosts; a bot challenge at robots.txt is read as 'allowed'; self-attested lifts for clauses requiring written consent (DC Inside - owner D1 to reconfirm); YouTube's derived-data rule unaddressed; ingest ignores most host stops; redirect loops lead to render captures; 'unknown' signed-in captures become public; word-only rate-limit/human-check notices stop only one URL; X has no terms entry. Danggeun is 'unchecked' honestly (no clause found; terms page unreadable here).
